stops.note: the Tungusic word for a spirit healer of eastern Siberia; its possible link to Sanskrit śramaṇa 'ascetic' via Chinese is disputed
the exiled Archpriest Avvakum's autobiography, written in the 1670s, describes a Siberian shaman's ritual, among the first Russian records of the word
Nicolaes Witsen's book on Siberia, Noord en Oost Tartarye (1692), spread the word and an engraving of a shaman across Europe
later extended by anthropologists to spirit healers in cultures worldwide

current_meaning: a person believed to contact the spirit world, especially to heal or divine
